newsitem.title: USA: Astronauts successfully grab telescope from orbit.
newsitem.headline: Astronauts successfully grab telescope from orbit.

text.p: Astronauts Tom Jones and Tamara Jernigan used shuttle Columbia's 50-foot (15.2 metre) robot arm early on Wednesday to latch onto a star-gazing telescope and begin hauling it back aboard for a return ride home.

Following a series of precise manoeuvres and rocket burns to rendezvous with the 7,000 pound (3,175 kg) telescope, the shuttle used its robot arm to grab it at 3:27 a.m. EST (0827 GMT). The crew planned to finish stowing the satellite inside the payload bay at 7:39 a.m. EST (1239 GMT), then prepare for return to earth on either Thursday or Friday.
"We have a good grapple on Orfeus-Spas," Jernigan said moments after using the robot arm to pluck the telescope out of its orbit.
The Orfeus-Spas telescope was released by the shuttle crew two weeks ago and flew in formation with Columbia, flying some 26 miles (40 km) behind the shuttle.

The German-made telescope was designed to collect data to help scientists learn more about the life cycle of stars, especially the gaseous, soupy matter that acts as a nursery for stars. The telescope is one of the largest ever deployed, ranking second only to the Hubble Telescope that remains in orbit.

The astronaut crew slowed Columbia with rocket thrusters early on Wednesday, then leapfrogged over the telescope to position the shuttle behind the Orfeus-Spas. Shuttle commander Ken Cockerell guided the orbiter to within about 35 feet (10.6 metres) for its retrieval.
